text:
sophia: Quick heads-up — onboarding run for magnet-13b-int4 on the longctx suite is showing small but consistent drift when KV-cache is warm and RoPE scale > 2.0. Noticed token-level divergence after ~2800 tokens.

raj: Can you paste the minimal repro? config + command?

sophia: repro below (shortened):
```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python tests/longctx_onboard.py \
  --model magnet-13b-int4 \
  --rope_scale 2.3 \
  --context 4096 \
  --use_kv_cache True \
  --quant_config configs/int4_default.json
```
Observed: fp16 vs int4 diff in generated token at pos ~2821: expected 'the' vs got 'a'.

lin: Interesting. Is it only with rope_scale > 2? Any diffs at 1.0/1.5?

sophia: At 1.0/1.5 tests are fine. At 2.0 small flakiness; 2.3 reproduces reliably.

sam: Do you have a short example input where it flips? Could paste the prompt and two outputs.

sophia: Short snippet: prompt = "In the experiment, the subject observed that"
fp16 continuation: "the value crept up..."
int4 continuation: "a value crept up..."

eval-bot: Eval summary uploaded: holdout-perplexity +1.8% (int4 vs fp16) on longctx-4k. Token-level mismatch spikes correlate with repeated prefixes and dense numeric spans. Full report: /evals/1762504321/report.html

lin: My first guess is RoPE index interpolation + quant rounding interacting with KV indexing. We saw similar off-by-one-like shifts when rotary phase was rescaled in the runtime before. Check the rotary index precompute path and the int4 dequant alignment.

raj: Also try disabling prefix caching (force cold KV) to see if it's a cache-coherence vs runtime math issue. If cold run matches fp16, it's likely a cache write/read mismatch.

sophia: I ran that: cold-run (clear kv) reduces diffs but doesn't fully eliminate them — suggests a compounding effect.

sam: I can reproduce locally with the above command + a diff script. Quick log of logits around token 2820 shows tiny shift in attention weights for head 7 layer 10.

lin: Can you dump kvcache keys for the two runs and compare fingerprints? Use debug kv dump (short):
```py
from runtime.debug import dump_kv_fingerprint
dump_kv_fingerprint(model, input_ids, out_path="/tmp/fp_int4.json")
```

sam: Did that. Fingerprints differ starting at step 68 (zero-indexed block), small numeric deltas in the rotary-cos/sin multiply results.

deploy-bot: Model packages used: magnet-13b-int4@v2026.03.15-rc and magnet-13b-fp16@v2026.02.28. Runtime kernel: kfloat-kernels@v2.9.

lin: Next experiments: (1) run int4 with fp16 rotary kernel (force fp16 ropemat ops) to isolate quantized matmul vs rotary math; (2) run int4 with kv-cache disabled; (3) run int4 + lower rope_scale to find threshold.

raj: I'll bisect runtime commits between x->y where we changed rotary precompute to see when the divergence started. Assigning to me.

sophia: Actionable:
- sam: attach the minimal prompt + diff script to thread (can you paste?)
- lin: prepare quick patch to force fp16 rotary ops inside int4 model for test
- raj: start bisect on runtime kernels
- eval-bot: re-run house-hold eval with rotary-forced test when available

sam: paste diff script:```py
# diff_gen.py (super short)
import subprocess, json
# run model1, model2, compare token sequences, print first mismatch
```
I'll attach full gist in a minute.

eval-bot: Got a trigger — queued a rotary-forced int4 job on the 4k longctx holdout (job id 1762504321-rt).

sophia: thanks — tagging @lin @raj — ping me if you want pair-debug later today. :eyes:

lin: I'll try the fp16-rotary patch now and post results here.

raj: starting bisect now, will update with a commit range if I find a repro commit.

sophia: great. low-priority note: include stress-run with repeated numeric sequences (we see spikes there) - might help reproduce faster.

sam: uploaded gist: https://gist.github.com/sam/rope-int4-diff-1762504321 (includes prompt + run + compare).

sophia: perfect. closing the loop — we'll reconvene when eval-bot posts results or raj has a bisect range.
